contexts.text: Every one is formed from the harmony of many things; and such as the harmony is, such is the one: a thing which is absolutely one cannot subsist; but only a harmonical one. Every Society in Heaven thus forms a one; and all the Societies together a one; and this from the Lord alone, through love. SE 2016.

Love to the Lord makes a man one with the Lord... so does charity... This one from love, the Lord describes in, I pray that they all may be one... that they may be one in Us... That they may be one, even as We are one ().
The whole earth was of one lip and one words () = that everywhere there was one doctrine in general and in particular.

In Heaven there are innumerable Societies, and all different, and yet they are one; for they are all led as a one by the Lord. (Just) as all the viscera, organs, and members, each of which acts in a different way... are governed as a one by the one soul... That these can thus act as a one, is from the fact that in Heaven there is one only influx, which is received by every individual according to his peculiar quality... and notwithstanding that the influx is only one, yet all things obey and follow as a one; and this through the mutual love in which they are. So it was in the first Ancient Church. Explained... There is one doctrine when all are in mutual love, or charity. Mutual love and charity make them one, although they are various; for they make a one out of the variety. All... have one end...
The people are one, and they all have one lip () = that they all had the truth of faith, and one doctrine.

A people is said to be one, and their lip one, when all have for an end the common good of society, of the Church, and the Lord's Kingdom; for thus the Lord is in the end, from whom all are a one. (The contrary state described.)
Hence the heavenly Societies are as a one; and this solely through mutual love from the Lord.
Evil Spirits... act as a one in persecuting truths and goods.
Still, the soul with the body make a one... AC 2018.
The principal and the instrumental... do indeed appear to be conjoined as if they were a one; but still they are not a one...
Hence the whole Heaven represents as it were one man...
Then man can make a one as to thought with those in Heaven.
That (the Divine) Trinity is a one. Illustrated.
The Rational and the Natural are to be conformed so as to make a one...
The infants did not as yet act as a one.
It is a common thing in the Word for one to represent many states which succeed...
That these (Divine Essentials) are one, is known to everyone within the Church.
The true men of the Church... adore... one...
They said... one God; but thought of three.
There are myriads of myriads of particulars in every little affection, and idea, which appear to man as one.
One () = so little as to be scarcely anything.

Conjugial love is mutual and reciprocal... so that they are as it were one... as is evident from... the two shall be for one flesh; therefore they are no more two, but one flesh (). AC 10169:end, Explained.
The Lord's Kingdom on earth consists of all who are in good, who, although scattered over the whole earth, are still one; and, as members, constitute one body.
Man was so created that his will and understanding should make a one...
Then the inmosts, the interiors, and the externals (of man) make a one.
I the will and understanding do not... make a one, the man has not been regenerated; that is, if good and truth... are not a one.
A New Church which is one in the Lord's Kingdom. Signified, Explained.
In ancient times there were many Churches... but still they made a one in this: that...
Then the Churches, however many, make a one; and each is then a one in the Lord's Kingdom.
So the innumerable Societies... constitute one Heaven...
In this case the several Churches do not make a one...

For man... cannot have an idea of one, unless he first has the idea of a number; for a one with man is formed from many: or, what is the same, from successive things [is formed] that which is simultaneous.

Yet of these innumerable varieties one Heaven is constituted... The one there is constituted of the many varieties so disposed by the Lord that they agree. The agreement or harmony of the many is imparted by the Lord through their all referring themselves to Him. (Explained.)
The celestial perceive that (the Divine Essentials) are one; but the spiritual remain in the idea of three, but want to think that they are one.
Although there were many, still they all thought and spoke as one; thus they all represented as one; and this because no one wanted to do anything from himself...

Afterwards were heard many choirs... but still they acted as one; for from the form of various things there resulted a one, in which was heavenly beauty. Thus the universal Heaven... can act as a one, by being in mutual love; for this they suffer themselves to be led by the Lord.
Myriads of myriads of things, which are perceived distinctly by those in a higher degree, appear as only one with those in a lower...
Still the dissent in the doctrinals of faith does not prevent the Church from being a one, if only there is unanimity in willing well and doing well. Example(s).
For perfection and strength are from the unanimous multitude of many, who act a one in a heavenly form...
(Thus) Heaven may, as it were, make a one with Hell... AC 3642, Explained.
Although the Hells are outside the Grand Man, they are nevertheless in this way reduced as it were into a one [with it], and are thus kept in order.
External things are images and forms compounded of myriads of internal things, which appear as a one.
The Societies, although innumerable and various, still act a one; as all things in the body, although various, [are] a one.
For things which are one, are presented as two in the sense of the letter.

For a one is never constituted of a number of same ones, or of things exactly similar; but of various things harmoniously conjoined: things various harmoniously conjoined present every one. So the goods and truths in the Spiritual World, although various, so as not to be exactly alike with one as with another, still make a one from the Divine, through love and charity, (which) are spiritual conjunction; and their variety is heavenly harmony, which makes such a concord that they are one in the Divine, that is, in the Lord.
The supreme sense is such that it appears divided in the sense of the letter, but is one in the supreme internal sense.
There is conjunction when (the Rational and the Natural) act a one; and they act a one when the Natural ministers...
These two Kingdoms are most distinct; but still in the Heavens they act a one.
The Lord then inflows into the affections of both (consorts) as into one affection.
Good, regarded in itself, is one; but it becomes various through truths...
For a one is never composed of identities; but of things various in a form; which make a one according to the form.
These three planes (in man) act as a one with the regenerate...
Every one consists of things various; and this through heavenly harmony and concord.
These two faculties (the will and the understanding) constitute a one. AC 5835.
These Societies (which correspond to the external man and to the internal man) in the Heavens, act a one; as, with man, do the regenerate external and internal man.
(An Angel) sees and feels innumerable things which he had before (when a Spirit) seen and felt as one.
To possess in the land = to make one; thus to consent.
Although the three are called one, still the thought distinguishes and makes three...
Unless (the use formed them and adapted them to itself) each and all the things in man would never conspire so unanimously to a one.
(Many) names together present and describe one Thing in the internal sense. Example(s).
When each and all things in man, and each and all things in nature, correspond to each other as do end, cause, and effect, they act a one. Explained.
In the other life there must be a concord and unanimity of all, so that they be a one, like each and all things in man...
This dream of Pharaoh is one () = that which is alike in both, which was foreseen. Explained. AC 5267.
By the servant who received one talent, are signified those who have received faith alone without charity.
One is not () = that the Divine Spiritual a quo does not appear; for Joseph is here the one. AC 5516.
For in Heaven there are perpetual varieties... and yet all are disposed into such a form that together they make a one...

One state is never exactly like another; nor does one Angel and Spirit pass through changes of state like those of another; for the reason that one is not exactly like another as to good and truth... but still from these various things the Lord makes a one. For it is a general canon, that every one, in which there is any quality, comes forth from things various, which by means of the agreement of harmony, are reduced into such an unanimity that they all appear as a one. Hence the one, or union, in the Heavens, is effected through love and charity. References.
At that time the Divine Human was not one with the Divine Itself... as when the Lord had made it in Himself altogether one. Illustrated.
This variety is more indefinite in the truths and goods which are of the Spiritual World, because one thing in the natural world corresponds to thousands and thousands in the Spiritual World...

In all angelic discourse there is a harmony as of singing, which in every termination ceases in a monosyllable; thus in a one... because each and all things in Heaven have relation to one God, as to their end.
The Societies there are all various, but the Lord conjoins all by means of the heavenly form, so that they are a one; for a one is made from things various suitably disposed into a form.
The scattered Societies (which constitute this order on earth) have been collected by the Lord, so that, like the Societies in Heaven, they represent one man.
That there is one God. Signified, Explained.

In one house it shall be eaten () = consociations of suitable goods, so that they make one good... The reason these (goods of the angelic Societies) make one good, is that every one comes forth not from one, but from many; for from many various but still accordant things is made a form which makes a one through a harmony; in Heaven, through a spiritual harmony, which is the good of love. References.
Ordination under generals, effects that the several things act a one...
There was not left in them even to one () = all and each.

There is such a communication in Heaven; and hence it is that they are a one; exactly as the organs, members, and viscera in man... by means of such communications present a one. Such a communication of goods is possible solely through love, which is spiritual conjunction...
On this side one, and on this side one () = on every side.
Thus these two (good and truth) are a one.
When, in the Word, one day is said, or one week, or one month, or one year, there is signified an entire period of time, or of state.
But these two lives (of the will and the understanding) with man are nevertheless one; and, when they are one, the things of faith are also of love, and those of love are also of faith...

It is said in the Church, that out of Three... there comes forth one Divine, which is also called one God... But the ideas of the men of the Church are founded upon three, but those of the Angels upon one... Hence (the former) can say that there is one God, but they can never think otherwise than that there are three, who by a union, which they call mystical, are one. In this way they can indeed think that there is one Divine, but not that there is one God... The one Divine is one by accordance; but the one God is altogether one...
One and a half = what is full. AC 9489. AC 9508. AC 9531. AC 9637.
One = something.
One curtain () = each of the several truths.
The habitation shall be one () = the whole Heaven thus completely a one.

For Heaven consists of myriads of Societies, and still the Lord leads them as one Angel, or as one man. The cause of this is that among them, all is mutual love from the Lord's love: when this love is among all, and in all, then all can be disposed into the heavenly form, which is such that many are a one; and the more there are, the more strongly are they a one. (So) with the innumerable things in the human body, which, although they are distinct and various, still make a one: the reason is that they are in a like form to that in which Heaven is...

The conjunction of the angelic Societies into one Heaven has relation to the following laws. 1. That every one in the form of the Heavens comes forth according to the heavenly harmony of a number of consociates. (Five more laws stated.)
Thou shalt join together the Tent so that it be one () = the external of Heaven thus completely a one.
For the Lord is in them, but not among them as one and distinct.

One order () = a trine there as a one... It is said as a one, because a one comes forth from three in successive order... Hence the three Heavens are a one in the ultimates; in like manner each Heaven. This derives its origin from the Divine Itself, in which a Trine... is a one. AC 9867. AC 9869. AC 9871.
It is said, one piece of bread, one cake, and one wafer (), because the Divine good, in itself, is one.
One Angel prevails against a thousand from the Hells.
Love so conjoins the Angels that in the Lord's sight all are as one.
The Lord thus effects that the three Heavens are a one.

Every one comes forth from things various; for a one which is not from things various is not anything; it has no form, and therefore no quality. But when a one comes forth from things various, and the various things are in a perfect form, in which each adjoins itself to the other as a friend accordant in a series, it then has a perfect quality. Heaven, too, is a one from things various ordinated in a most perfect form. Explained.
As Heaven is such, it is ruled by the Lord as... a one...

The reason so many varied things act in man a one, is that there is not anything there which does not... perform a use: the whole performs a use to its parts, and the parts to the whole... and therefore they provide for each other, mutually respect each other, and are conjoined in such a form, that all and each relate to the whole and its good. Hence it is that they act a one.
Hence those in the Heavens act a one; but this not from themselves, but from the Lord... Signified.
Hence two consorts are not called two, but one Angel.

Every one is formed from the harmonious consensus of many; and it is such a one as is this consensus. Thus is it that every Society of Heaven makes a one; and that all the Societies of Heaven make a one; and this from the Lord alone, by means of love.
From this universal and singular regard (all the things in the body) act as a one.
The interior thought acts a one with the exterior through correspondence... But with those in evil (they do) not act a one...
The thought then makes a one with the will; and such a one that it scarcely appears (to the Spirit) that he is thinking, but that he is willing; and almost the same hen he is speaking.
With these, the Internal and External act a one; as do the effecting cause and the effect; or as do the prior and the posterior.

From this order in creation it may be evident that such is the containing nexus from primes to ultimates, that, regarded together, they constitute a one, in which the prior cannot be separated from the posterior...
(Thus) the human race and the angelic Heaven make a one...
Heaven is of all forms the most perfect; and the more there are in it, the more is there given a direction and consensus to a one...
The quality of every form is from the ordination together of the varied things therein; and from their mutual respect; and from the consensus to a one; from which every form is considered as a one...
That God is one... General article. TCR 6.
It is customary in the Word to mention two Divines, and sometimes three, which yet are one... Illustrated.
Consequently, God is one in Person and in Essence... DFaith 35. AR 67. BE 116. TCR 2.
The Word in the sense of the letter is such, that the things which are one are distinguished as if they were not one...
Charity and faith make a one, like the will and the understanding... like affection and thought... and like good and truth.
That Esse and Existere in God Man are distinctly one. General article.
That in God Man infinite things are distinctly one. General article.
In man there are innumerable things, but still man feels them as a one. Enumerated, Explained.
That there is one God Man from whom all things are. General article.
That spiritual heat and light... make a one, as His Divine Love and Divine wisdom make a one. General article.

All spiritual things which originate through the heat and light of their Sun, regarded in themselves, in like manner make a one; but, regarded as proceeding from the affections of the Angels, they do not make a one.
Love and wisdom proceed as a one from the Lord, but are not received as a one by the Angels.
That the Divine Love and the Divine wisdom proceed from the Lord as a one. General article.
That there is no such thing as a one without a form; but that the form itself makes the one. Explained, Example(s).
That a form makes a one the more perfectly, in proportion as the things which enter into the form are distinctly different, and yet united. Explained.
That this one is, in a certain image, in every created thing. General article.
That it is of the Divine Providence that every created thing, in general and in part, should be such a one... General article.
One cannot be changed unless all are.
Suppose a one from whom all things are; are they not all that one's from whom they depend in order...
Such are not able to say one God. (Shown by experiment.)
(Many clergy who appeared as one great figure.)
Five have fallen, and one is ()... One is = the following Divine truth, that...
(An angelic conversation concerning the one God.)
The Divine Esse is one, the Same Itself, and Indivisible; thus so is the Divine Essence...
(At a distance the two consorts appeared as one Angel.)
Their love grows every day into conjunction, even so that they are no longer two, but as a one.
In Heaven two consorts are not called two, but one Angel: this is meant by They are no more two, but one flesh. 177, Explained.

I said, Ye two are one; and the man replied. We are one: her life is in me, and mine in her: we are two bodies, but one soul: the union between us is like that of the heart and lungs; she is my heart, and I am her lungs...
In these two (the truth of good, and the good of truth) there has been implanted from creation an inclination to conjoin themselves into a one. Explained.
That conjugial love conjoins two souls and thence minds into a one. Explained.
That those who are in love truly conjugial feel themselves a united man, and as one flesh. Explained.
To the end that the will of both may become one; and that thus they both may become one man. (Explained.)
That those who are in love truly conjugial continually want to be one man; but that those who are not want to be two. Explained.

That the souls of two unite themselves, when love for the sex is restricted to one woman or one man of the sex... is clearly evident from the fact, that the lives of both unite themselves; consequently their souls...
That love and wisdom in God make a one. General article.
That the essence of love is to love others outside of itself; to want to be one with them... General article. TCR 43:3. TCR 46:2.
The universal Heaven, together with the Church on earth, is as one man...
That there is one God, who is a Man...
That the truths of faith, however numerous they are, and however diverse they appear, make a one from the Lord... General article.
That the Lord, charity, and faith, make a one, like the life, will, and understanding in man... General article. TCR 576.
The universal human race, from the first creation, must form a one...
She desired to become one with him as to the body also, which also took place. (See Marriage.)
One is predicated of good, and three, of truths; and by one, when predicated of good, is signified what is perfect; thus also what is genuine.

No more two, but one flesh = that thus the understanding of good and truth, and the affection of good and truth, are not two, but one; in like manner as the will and the understanding are indeed two, but still are one; in like manner as are truth and good, and also charity and faith, which indeed are two, but still are one, namely, when truth is of good, and good is of truth; and when faith is of charity, and charity is of faith.

For good and truth inmostly love each other, and burn to be united as into a one: the reason is that the Divine good and the Divine truth proceed united from the Lord, and therefore must be united in an Angel and a man of the Church. This unition is never possible except by the marriage of two minds into a one... For two consorts who are in conjugial love from the Lord... although apparently two, are actually one; they are two as to bodies, but one as to life; as... with the eyes, which are two as to organs, but one as to sight... and therefore in Heaven two consorts are not called two Angels, but one.
The origin of these delights is from the fact that the consorts want to be united, as to their minds, into a one, and that Heaven conspires into such a union...
The consorts pass the night in each other's bosoms, as if they had been created into one.

Love truly conjugial is not possible except between two; as neither is the Lord's love towards Heaven, which is one from Him and in Him; or towards the Church, which also is one from Him and in Him; for all in the Heavens, and in the Church, must be one through mutual love from love to the Lord: the Angel in Heaven, and the man in the Church, who does not in this way make one with the rest, is not from Heaven, neither is of the Church.

The man communicates his soul to his wife by actual love... hence the two become one; and then each and all things in the body of the one have regard to their mutual in that of the other. This is genuine marriage, possible only between two. Explained.
When, therefore, the two minds act a one, then also the two bodies are so united potentially, that they are no more two, but one flesh. To want to become one flesh is conjugial love...

There are consorts in the Heavens who are in such conjugial love, that both can be one flesh, and they are so when they want, and they then appear as one man. I have seen, and I have spoken with them, and they have said that they have one life... and are as the pairs (of organs) in man...
In one hour () = suddenly; here, also, everything; thus, total. Explained.
That which is thus universal is perceived no otherwise than as a one; and a one without a singular perception of singulars is obscure...
